title: Cross-language starter handbook: resilient streaming + retry patterns for server & CLI
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Deliver a set of small, opinionated starter templates and cookbook snippets that demonstrate robust streaming ergonomics and retry strategies across TypeScript (Next.js), Python (FastAPI), and Go (HTTP server + CLI). Aim is to reduce onboarding time for engineering customers integrating Redwood’s streaming and chunked-generation surfaces while codifying recommended backoff, cancellation, and resumability patterns.

Goals:
- Provide 4 runnable starters: Next.js incrementally-rendering app (SSE/Edge-friendly), FastAPI streaming endpoint for server-worker integration, Go HTTP server demonstrating kv-cache-friendly batching and graceful shutdown, and a small cross-platform CLI demonstrating chunked uploads + progress and resume semantics.
- Include cookbook snippets: token budgeting, exponential backoff with jitter, resumable KV-cache keys for partial responses, typed streaming listener in TS, generator-based streaming consumer in Python, and context-aware cancellation in Go.
- Surface common telemetry hooks (trace IDs, latency buckets, token counts) and sample unit/integration tests.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Each starter is a minimal repo (2-3 files) with README, runnable with a single command (npm start / uvicorn / go run).
2) Examples include both client and server patterns where relevant (Next.js client pulling SSE, FastAPI server streaming with background writer, Go server + CLI showing resume).
3) Examples demonstrate robust retry/backoff: idempotent chunk identifiers, exponential backoff with full jitter, and clear guidance when to retry versus when to fail fast.
4) CI checks: lint + unit tests + a smoke integration test that runs a local mock of the Redwood runtime to validate streaming boundaries and retry behavior.
5) Docs: short cookbook.md summarizing patterns, code snippets copy-paste ready, and a compatibility matrix for SDK versions (python>=0.6, ts-sdk>=1.2, go-sdk>=0.4).

Non-goals:
- Not implementing production-grade deploy scripts or infra. Keep repos intentionally tiny for onboarding.

Technical notes / suggestions:
- Next.js example: server route that proxies Redwood streaming responses and re-emits as SSE. Client shows incremental hydration and a small RetryButton that uses opaque resume tokens. Use TypeScript types for partial-response unions.
- FastAPI example: dependency-injected background writer that flushes to SSE/HTTP chunking; demonstrates how to attach trace IDs and how to handle client disconnects gracefully (cancellation + requeue).
- Go example: http.Handler that uses a streaming decoder over bytes.Reader, writes checkpoints to an in-memory kv interface (simulated), and demonstrates graceful shutdown with inflight request draining. Provide a companion CLI that can request resume tokens and re-request missing chunks.
- Cookbook: include snippet for token budgeting pseudo-code; show server-side gating when request would exceed per-request token budget and how to fallback to shorter model or truncated context.

Dependencies / Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.dev/display/ENG/streaming-starter-kits (draft)
- Mock runtime repo for CI (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/mock-stream-runtime/pull/113 (WIP)
- Example PR placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/429

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: examples leak internal helper APIs that will break with future SDK changes. Mitigation: only use public, stable SDK surfaces and include a compatibility note and tests pinned to SDK versions.
- Risk: UX differs across runtimes (Node ESM vs Go modules). Mitigation: keep examples idiomatic per language and call out differences in cookbook.md.
